title: structRFM — RNA secondary-structure prediction
description: Run the structure-guided RNA foundation model structRFM on an RNA sequence and return its last-layer attention map — an L×L learned representation that correlates with base pairing (including crossing/pseudoknot interactions a nested dot-bracket would discard). It is a model representation, not a calibrated secondary-structure prediction.
citation: Zhu et al., An open structure-guided RNA foundation model for generalizable prediction. Nature (2026). https://github.com/heqin-zhu/structRFM

fields.name: sequence
fields.label: RNA sequence
fields.help: A single RNA sequence over A/C/G/U (N allowed for unknown positions).

fields.name: seed
fields.label: Seed
fields.help: Prediction is deterministic; seed is accepted for reproducibility bookkeeping.

example_summary: A tiny 12-nucleotide RNA hairpin (GGGGAAAACCCC), bundled so you can try the pipeline without supplying a sequence.
example_details: A hand-picked minimal hairpin (GGGGAAAACCCC): four G-C pairs closing a four-base loop. It exercises the sequence -> attention-map path end to end. Swap in any single RNA sequence over A/C/G/U. Real inference returns structRFM's last-layer mean attention (an L×L matrix); the stub returns a deterministic placeholder matrix (engine=stub).
notes: Real inference uses structRFM's programmatic API (structRFM.infer.structRFM_infer) with the base pretrained checkpoint (GitHub release structRFM_checkpoint.tar.gz, MIT) — NOT the upstream SSP script, whose imports (param_turner2004/utils) are not in the documented install. Output is the last-layer mean attention map, a learned representation that correlates with base pairing (incl. pseudoknots), not a calibrated SSP prediction; a true dot-bracket head is deferred (would need mxfold2's param_turner2004). source_commit, checkpoint_digest, worker_image_digest and max_length stay provisional until confirmed by a Runpod smoke run. The runner reports engine=structRFM vs engine=stub.
